assign.now: corpus.js + corpus/page.js live: 23 agree, 1 disagrees, 6 n/a — and it found three real defects in the tier on its first run.

log.msg: The corpus found three real defects in the tier before it validated anything. width-used could not see a narrow body — it spanned leftmost to rightmost content, so one full-bleed topbar pinned the answer to the whole screen however narrow the column under it was; it is the median of per-row spans now. frame-gap and pad-share could not see a stripped layout — a page carries a dozen correctly-padded components and two or three layout tracks, so the MEDIAN moved by nothing when every tracks inset was removed; both are width-weighted now. And a transform bug of my own that is worth the same warning: appending a token to the end of a spec line puts it in the PART half, so `basis pad > menu` + ` tone` reads as the part menu with a count of tone — the layout still renders, the token does nothing, and three cases quietly measured zero change.

Three design points the corpus forced, each after getting it wrong first. (1) A pair only means something if the LEFT side is actually good: unbounding --measure:52em changed nothing at any width because 52em already runs ~117 characters a line here, so the case was comparing two broken layouts — cases now carry a base that fixes the subject before the break breaks it. (2) A band with nothing to measure is n/a, not a failure — slivers reads null on a dashboard of tiles, and scoring that as a failure made the corpus look broken when it was silent. (3) Two cases are EXPECTED TO FAIL and they are the most useful two: hid-the-text is invisible to all eleven bands because every one is geometry, and scrambled-the-spacing cannot be reached from a layout at all because a pages gap vocabulary belongs to its components. A corpus with no declared boundary reads as a claim that the tier catches everything.

assign.outcome: **[/framework/ext/LayoutTool/taste/corpus/](/framework/ext/LayoutTool/taste/corpus/) — the taste tier can now be wrong.** Six named breaks x five presets, judged on the band each case names rather than on the total: **23 agree, 1 disagrees, 6 not applicable**. Two cases are expected to FAIL and are the most useful two — they mark where the tier stops seeing (colour, and a pages gap vocabulary). It found three real defects in the tier on its first run: width-used could not see a narrow body behind a full-bleed topbar (now a median of per-row spans), and frame-gap and pad-share could not see a stripped layout because the median hid it (now width-weighted). The one disagreement is recorded as a decision rather than a bug: a break that costs a band at 3440 and helps it at 390 averages out. The tiers first Open item is narrowed, not closed — this validates the ORDER, and the PLACE of each band still needs a person.
